trust_decision.summary: Extractor-generated HTML is only trusted after it has been re-parsed and stripped of on*/srcdoc/dangerous-URI attributes inside buildExtractorResponse, before it becomes response.content; at the pinned commit that decision is made nowhere for extractor output — resolveContentUrls only rewrites relative URLs, while sanitization exists only for the non-extractor pipeline (standardize attribute allowlist) and the fallback body.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'unescaped attribute interpolation in site extractors' and the fix's own regression test drives the X article header image; the page-read alt is interpolated into a double-quoted attribute with no escaping, and src comes straight from the page too.

buildExtractorResponse() — the one builder both parse() (line 843) and parseAsync() (line 731) go through; the fix turns its resolveContentUrls call into a parse + _stripUnsafeElements + resolveRelativeUrls pass (fix.diff:57-64)
